main_text.p: admodum lætantibus, gaudente rege, benigne a filio susceptus. Id gestum anno ætatis Gen.47.iacob centesimo & tricesimo: a diluvio autem anno Mccc & lx. Cæterum ab eo tempore quo Abrahã in terra Chanaanæorum consedit, in id quod Iacob Ægyptum ingressus est, referuntur anni CCxv. feptimo decimoIgitur Iacob septimo & decimo anno quâ Ægypto advenerat, urgente morbo, Sig.[?]Ioseph filium obtestatur, corpus sepulcro suo redderet. Tum Ioseph patri benedicendos filios suos obtulit: quibus benedictis cum tamē benedictionis merito maiori minorem præposuisset, filios omnes Gen.48.benedictione lustravit. Gen.49.Decessit autē annos natus cxLvii. Funus magnifice curatum. Gen.50.Corpus in sepulcro maiorū Ioseph condidit. Fratres post patris obitum pro conscientia paventes, benigne habuit. Gen.51.Decessit autem Ioseph ipse ætatis anno decimo & centesimo. Hebræi igitur qui in Exod.1.Ægyptum devenerant, incredibile memoratu est, quam cito numero auctifint, multiplicataque progenie Ægyptum repleverint. Sed defuncto rege, qui eos ob seruitus Ægyptimeritū Ioseph benigne fovebat, succes-tium regū imperio deprimebantur. Nam &c.

page.notes: The page is one continuous block of text with no visible paragraph indents, so it is given as one paragraph. The marginal note "Sig.[?]" is uncertain. The margin text "feptimo / decimo" is set as one note. The Roman numerals "CCxv" and "cxLvii" are copied as printed. The page number is printed as "2o" in the scan and is given here as 20. The word "Mccc & lx" reads "lx" in the scan. The word "succes-tium" is a line-end break with the rest of the word "succedentium" on the following line. The text on the right edge of the scan is cut off, so the final word of the last line may be incomplete.
